lecture_04.title: CS336 Spring 2026, Lecture 4: Attention alternatives and mixtures of experts
lecture_04.anchor_convention: lecture_04.pdf:p<page>, page numbers from `pdftotext -layout` form feeds (title slide = p1; 60 pages)
lecture_04.note: Evidence is the text layer of the slides (lecture_04.txt), extracted page-by-page by discover_slides.py. The deck is figure-heavy: the context-cost plot (p2), the local/global attention and systems-engineering panels (p3), the hybrid-model result tables (p6, p8, p10, p11), the DSA diagram (p12-p13), every MoE scaling/ablation plot (p16-p23, p28, p33-p34, p43, p49), the routing diagrams (p27, p29-p31), the balancing-loss formulas (p40-p42), the parallelism diagrams (p44-p46), the stability plot (p48) and the DeepSeek architecture diagrams (p54-p59) have no numbers in the text layer; where a KP relies on such a figure its filtering_note says so. The only numbers in the text are: the linear-attention FLOP counts (p4), hybrid ratios 7-to-1 and 3-1 (p6, p8, p10), the k values and expert table (p29, p35), the per-expert derivative on p40, SFT size 1.4M (p50), upcycling configs (p52-p53) and the DeepSeek v1/v2/v3 sizes (p54-p56). Note that this deck does not cover MQA/GQA, sliding-window attention beyond the phrase 'local + global', or capacity factor by name; MQA/GQA are in lecture 3.
